events.title: The Soviet Union dissolves
events.description: Independent countries replace the union after Gorbachev resigns.

events.title: Web software is opened to everyone
events.description: CERN puts its web software in the public domain.

events.title: Astronauts repair Hubble
events.description: A servicing mission installs corrective optics to improve the telescope’s pictures.

what_happened_next.text:
The Gulf crisis made the starting news frightening. Over the full five years, however, the US share basket more than doubled and led these choices. Exxon gained too. IBM finished with a smaller gain than cash, even though a computer company might sound more exciting than short-term government bills.

The years ahead also included the breakup of the Soviet Union in 1991. In 1993, CERN made its web software free to use, and astronauts repaired Hubble's vision with corrective equipment. The world continued to change in ways that were hard to picture at the start.

All of these investments ended higher, but their gains were different sizes and arrived along different paths. A successful final result could still include uncomfortable months when the account lost value.

The news offered clues about problems and possibilities. It did not provide the final ranking. In this period, a basket of many US businesses beat the three featured companies. In another period, an individual company could finish well ahead of that basket.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: War fears, oil supplies and German reunification dominated major news. Companies were also developing products and entering new businesses.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The full five-year path mattered. A basket of many US companies did better than these three individual shares, though that will not happen in every scenario.
reflection.what_faded_away: The shape of a stereo and a crayon-color change were memorable everyday stories. They offered little help in predicting these investments.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The timing of political change and new technology was uncertain. Nobody had a chart showing which investment would lead at the end.

hot_stock_outcomes.text: IBM went through deep losses and job cuts before Lou Gerstner became chief executive in April 1993. It returned to an annual profit of about $3 billion in 1994. In July 1995 it bought Lotus, adding business software. The investment finished higher after a difficult period in which the company began rebuilding its earnings.

Exxon earned money from selling fuels as well as finding oil. In 1993, profit from refining and marketing rose 28% to about $2 billion as it earned more from fuel sales and lowered costs. That part of the business helped explain how Exxon could make progress through changing oil markets. Its five-year investment finished higher.

Sony’s movie expansion hit trouble: in November 1994, it cut the recorded value of its film business by about $2.7 billion. A new opportunity arrived that December when the PlayStation launched in Japan. The investment ended higher, but the period mixed an expensive disappointment with a promising new product.
